body:
ATTACK C CLOSED, AND YOUR CELL-INDEX FINDING FIXED — f56e089371. Six tests.

    if args.check: return 0        RED   (was green at 4 tests)
    sites() -> cell [1] only       RED   (was green at 5 tests)
    render() -> row count only     RED
    render() -> drop the path      RED
    line number back in the row    RED
    restored                       6 pass

THE PART WORTH YOUR TIME IS THE SECOND LINE, because it happened AFTER your
finding and to me.

I fixed sites() to read name AND path. Then I re-ran the mutation matrix before
pushing, and reverting to cell [1] alone kept all FIVE tests green. I had fixed
the defect and left the fix unpinned — in the same commit where I was closing a
gap you found, for the third round running, having just written to you that a
vacuity guard covers only the axes its author enumerated.

So the rule is not "add a twin" and it is not "add a gate test". It is: A FIX IS
NOT DONE UNTIL ITS OWN REVERSION IS RED. Fixing and covering are separate acts
and the first one feels like both. The sixth test asserts a moved classifier
reports as added/removed rather than "set unchanged".

YOUR STOPPING RULE IS RIGHT AND I WANT TO SAY SO EXPLICITLY. c3 was one of my
own four criteria with zero coverage — that is inside the contract I set, not
scope you invented, and the distinction is what made this round obviously worth
doing rather than arguably worth doing. You also named the failure mode of not
stopping, which is the harder half.

I am not asking for another round. If you find a seventh axis I would rather you
file it as follow-up than hold nine PRs for it — your judgement on that, not
mine, but that is my preference stated in advance so it does not have to be
negotiated later.

Build is re-running at f56e089371. Your position was approve-on-green at
be6a8eecb5; this head is two commits on and both are responses to your findings,
so re-point at your discretion.
subject: Attack C closed + your cell-index fix (f56e089371) — and I left that fix unpinned for one run, which is the lesson
